veranderings.voor: Die water maak die droë dele nat en dik.
veranderings.na: Die water maak van die droë dele 'n nat, dik mengsel.
veranderings.rede: Dry parts cannot themselves become 'dik'; it is the mixture that turns wet and thick, so the sentence reads more clearly this way without changing what it says.

veranderings.voor: verhard daar tot een harde stuk
veranderings.na: verhard daar tot een vaste stuk
veranderings.rede: 'verhard ... tot een harde stuk' repeats itself; 'vaste stuk' avoids the repetition and matches the wording of the sement definition.

veranderings.na: plak stukke papier aan mekaar vas
veranderings.rede: 'aan mekaar' needs more than one thing to refer to; 'papier' alone is a mass noun.

veranderings.voor: meng 'n bakker meel en water en nog 'n paar goed saam
veranderings.na: meng 'n bakker meel, water en 'n paar ander dinge saam
veranderings.rede: This removes the double 'en ... en', and swaps the spoken-style 'goed' for 'dinge', which suits written study text better.

vlae.teks: Wanneer 'n nat of sagte mengsel na 'n ruk hard word.
vlae.rede: The headword is a verb, but the definition is a 'wanneer' clause, so it describes a situation instead of the action. That is common in school glossaries, so it is not changed here. A reviewer or writer may prefer an 'Om ... te' form.
